title: The greater beasts
summary: Creatures of myth, faded from the world but kept alive by belief.

claims.text: The greater beasts are the creatures of fable, from gryphons and unicorns to krakens and manticores, which have almost entirely left the mortal world.
Where they came from matters less than that people believed in them; while that faith lasts, such beasts take their origin from humanity and can be found by anyone who looks hard enough.
Many are as intelligent and passionate as people, with long lives and goals that make little sense in human terms.

title: Cockatrice
summary: A venomous bird-serpent hatched from the last basilisk.

claims.text: The first cockatrice came from a rooster that ate the last basilisk; it kills with a glance, with its breath or with the incurable venom of its hooked serpent tail.

Cockatrices are sexless and breed by stinging a rooster, which lays the egg; as magic waned they began stinging other animals and even humans, who fall sick until the egg passes and suffer bad dreams ever after.
The last mortal record of one is a Warsaw church entry from 1587. Survivors now lurk in rural Chantries and unsettled Realms, where they plague mages in their sanctuaries.
One tale holds that Chimera cursed the cockatrice for twisting a riddle, and that it fled into the Wyrm's coils out of spite.
